The doctor you are referring to is **Dr. Li Wenliang**. He was an ophthalmologist at Wuhan Central Hospital who, in late December 2019, warned his colleagues about a cluster of pneumonia cases resembling SARS, which he believed were caused by a new coronavirus. For this early warning, he was reprimanded by local authorities for "spreading rumors."

Dr. Li Wenliang later contracted COVID-19 while treating patients and passed away on **February 7, 2020**. His death sparked widespread public grief and discussions about transparency and freedom of speech in China during the early stages of the pandemic.

# Dr. Li Wenliang

**Dr. Li Wenliang** was the Wuhan ophthalmologist who tried to warn colleagues about a new SARS-like virus in late December 2019, based on cases he observed at Wuhan Central Hospital.

## Key details:

- **Warning:** On December 30, 2019, he posted a message in a private WeChat group warning fellow doctors about a cluster of cases resembling SARS, advising them to take protective measures.

- **Reprimand:** In early January 2020, Wuhan police summoned him and forced him to sign a statement admitting he had made "false comments" that had "severely disturbed the social order." He was accused of spreading rumors.

- **Infection:** He later contracted COVID-19 himself, likely while treating patients, including one with glaucoma who turned out to be infected.

- **Death:** He died on **February 7, 2020**, at Wuhan Central Hospital, sparking widespread public grief and anger across China.

- **Aftermath:** His death led to an outpouring of criticism on Chinese social media regarding the handling of early warnings, despite censorship efforts. In March 2020, Chinese authorities posthumously exonerated him and the Wuhan Public Security Bureau formally apologized to his family, acknowledging the reprimand was improper.

Li Wenliang became a symbol of the human cost of delayed information-sharing in the early COVID-19 outbreak and is often remembered as a whistleblower who tried to protect public health.
